messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: HMM_precipitation_amount
parts:
What you need to implement for HMMs depends on your
inferential goals. Which HMM architecture and set of
distributions you want to use depend on the application
model. HMMs are a rather vaguely defined class of limited-memory
time-series models.

I don't know anything about precipitation, either in
chemistry or meteorology, so you'd need to say more about
what you're trying to do. Is there a reference model someone
defined in a book or paper that you're trying to implement
in Stan?

Also, HMMs are a difficult entry point into Bayesian inference.
Without a lot of supervised data, they tend to have highly
multi-modal posteriors, and even with supervised data have issues
with index identifiability. That, and to make them efficient enough
requires a lot of index fiddling in the Viterbi and/or forward-backward
algorithms.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: HMM_precipitation_amount
parts:
You don't need to use EM to fit an HMM in Stan.
There are examples in the manual of discrete output
HMMs that can be fit with MCMC. I'll let you be
the judge of whether the doc is clear --- HMMs
are tricky to describe in both words and code.

You could also use Stan's optimizer instead of EM if
you want a posterior mode.

There are examples in the manual of how to use the
Viterbi algorithm for first-best state predictions.

- Bob
